name: Scotch Game
description: A beginner-friendly open game that teaches central pawn breaks, active development, and simple tactical play after 1.e4 e5.

branches.title: Main Line: Break With d4
branches.description: Learn the default Scotch idea: develop, then challenge the center with d4.

moves.title: Claim the center
moves.explanation: Controls d5 and f5 while opening lines for the bishop and queen.

moves.title: Black mirrors
moves.explanation: Black also takes central space, creating an open-game structure.

moves.title: Develop with pressure
moves.explanation: Develops a knight and attacks e5 before making the central break.

moves.title: Black defends e5
moves.explanation: Black develops and protects the e5 pawn.

moves.title: Break open the center
moves.explanation: d4 challenges e5 and opens lines. The Scotch teaches active central play after development.

hints: The key training move in this branch is d4.
Follow the highlighted move and keep your plan simple.
coachingNotes: Learn the default Scotch idea: develop, then challenge the center with d4.

branches.title: Recapture and Develop
branches.description: If Black accepts the central break, recapture calmly and keep developing.

moves.title: Recommended: recapture
moves.explanation: Nxd4 centralizes the knight and keeps White developed. Avoid queen recaptures that lose time.

hints: The key training move in this branch is Nxd4.
Follow the highlighted move and keep your plan simple.

branches.title: Meet Pressure With Nc3
branches.description: If Black attacks e4 with Nf6, defend through development.

moves.title: Black counterattacks
moves.explanation: Black attacks e4 instead of defending e5.

moves.title: Recommended: develop and defend
moves.explanation: Nc3 protects e4 and develops a new piece. Simple development solves the problem.

hints: The key training move in this branch is Nc3.

branches.title: Continue With d4
branches.description: If Black develops the bishop, use d4 to challenge the center.

moves.title: Black develops bishop
moves.explanation: Black points toward f2 and develops actively.

moves.title: Recommended: central break
moves.explanation: d4 challenges the center before Black gets too comfortable. Keep development active.
